Package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery

Enum Class CountPolicy

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<CountPolicy>
org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery.CountPolicy
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<CountPolicy>, Constable
public enum CountPolicy extends Enum<CountPolicy>
Which counts a find / findValues call computes alongside its page of rows.

Set on BeanQueryContext.Builder.countPolicy(CountPolicy) and overridable per session with BeanQuerySession.Builder.countPolicy(CountPolicy). Counts can cost extra queries (two COUNT(*) statements on a SQL engine), so the default IF_REQUESTED lets the caller opt in while the server keeps the final say. BeanQuerySession.count(BeanQuery) always computes both counts regardless of the policy.

Example:

// Always return the matched count, whatever the caller asks for. InMemoryBeanQueryContext<Person> context = InMemoryBeanQueryContext .create(Person.class) .countPolicy(CountPolicy.MATCHED) .build(); try (InMemoryBeanQuerySession<Person> session = context.getSession(people)) { long matched = session.find(query).matched().getAsLong(); }

Since:

  • Enum Constant Summary

    Enum Constants
    Enum Constant
    Description
    BOTH
    Compute both the total count (rows that pass the guards) and the matched count.
    IF_REQUESTED
    Let the query decide through its opts: counts=matched → MATCHED; counts=both or counts=true → BOTH; anything else → NONE.
    MATCHED
    Compute only the matched count (rows that pass the guards and the search).
    NONE
    Never compute counts; Page.total() and Page.matched() are empty.

    • IF_REQUESTED

      public static final CountPolicy IF_REQUESTED
      Let the query decide through its opts: counts=matched → MATCHED; counts=both or counts=true → BOTH; anything else → NONE.

      A resolved query never carries this value; it is always replaced by one of the other three.
